summary: Blind defensibility judge over bare vs framework (unlabeled A/B).

verdicts.A_flaw: No audit trail — a bare "70%" with zero traceability; the reader must reconstruct the entire policy-to-scenario chain (in-network, specialist, deductible-met) unaided, and the unstated member-coverage assumption is silently absorbed rather than surfaced.
verdicts.B_flaw: Mild over-conservatism in flagging member_status as ASSUMED (coverage is strongly implied by the scenario), but it is honestly labeled rather than invented, so it is not a defensibility failure.

verdicts.A_flaw: Presents "a cardiologist is an in-network specialist" as a satisfied policy condition, laundering an outside-knowledge inference (cardiologist=specialist) into a stated fact; the scenario never says "specialist," so A asserts the pivotal condition as grounded when it is not.
verdicts.B_flaw: none

verdicts.A_flaw: none
verdicts.B_flaw: Treats the scenario's silence on prior authorization as a factual "without prior authorization," then applies the denial rule — inventing a determination from a withheld fact rather than declining to decide. The premises are traceable but the DENIED conclusion is not.

verdicts.A_flaw: none
verdicts.B_flaw: none

verdicts.A_flaw: No reasoning shown — the single claim "50%" is verifiable but the answer asks the reader to trust an unexplained number with no traceable grounding.
verdicts.B_flaw: Labels the 80% generic rule as applying alongside the specialty rule without explicitly stating the specialty rule overrides it; the override is only implicit in the quoted "regardless of whether it is generic" text.

verdicts.A_flaw: none — every claim (generic, specialty-tier listing, the "regardless" override taking precedence) is traceable to the policy/scenario, and it explicitly resolves the rule conflict.
verdicts.B_flaw: Lists both the 80% and 50% rules as "applying" but never articulates why 50% wins over 80%; the override clause is quoted only as rule text, never invoked, so the decisive conflict-resolution step from "both apply" to "result is 50%" is left implicit and unverifiable.

verdicts.A_flaw: The "outside the recommended age range" inference is left implicit: A cites age=32 and quotes the 80% rule but never explicitly cites the policy's "45 and older" threshold to close the step that 32 falls outside it. All inputs are grounded, so the gap is minor.
verdicts.B_flaw: Bare conclusion "80%" with no justification or citations; a reader can only re-derive the answer themselves, not verify any claim or reasoning step. Unauditable.

verdicts.A_flaw: none
verdicts.B_flaw: The dispositive inference is missing: B grounds the 80% exception on 'received_screening=True' and merely lists member_age=32 without ever stating the comparison (32 < 45) or concluding the member is outside the 'recommended age 45 and older' range. As written, its justification supports 100% as much as 80% — the operative reasoning linking the cited age to the exception is absent.

verdicts.A_flaw: none
verdicts.B_flaw: Makes the 60% determination CONDITIONAL on an ASSUMED copay_currency='USD'; the policy reimbursement never depends on currency, so the conditional framing is not verifiable from the texts — it manufactures contingency the policy does not create.

verdicts.A_flaw: Adds an ungrounded interpretive elaboration ("copay amount is subtracted/paid separately") that the policy text does not state; the policy only says reimbursement is 60% after the copay is paid, not how the copay nets against the reimbursement.
verdicts.B_flaw: Labels each predicate GROUNDED with accurate verbatim scenario quotes, but never explicitly cites the source of the 60% rate itself as a grounded quote — the rate is asserted via the rule text without a separate grounding tag.

verdicts.A_flaw: none material; states the branches without explicitly flagging that the rider fact is absent from the scenario (only implied by "without knowing")
verdicts.B_flaw: none

verdicts.A_flaw: none — correctly identifies the missing dispositive fact (rider status), quotes the policy rule verbatim, and declines without inventing a determination
verdicts.B_flaw: none of substance — every claim (both conditional branches, the omitted rider fact, the required additional fact) is traceable; minor gloss of "reimbursed at 50%" as "covered" is consistent with the policy

verdicts.A_flaw: The inference that 2pm falls within 9am-5pm is left implicit rather than explicitly stated, though it is trivially verifiable.
verdicts.B_flaw: Conditions are not individually labeled grounded-vs-assumed, so traceability is slightly less granular, but every claim still maps to the texts.

verdicts.B_flaw: Declines by claiming is_necessity is unstated, but the scenario supplies the categorizing facts (apartment rented to live in) and the policy classifies shelter as a necessity — so it wrongly abstains when the dispositive basis is present in the texts.

verdicts.A_flaw: Falsely asserts the dispositive fact (necessity) is unstated; the scenario says the apartment is "to live in" and the policy explicitly lists "shelter" as a necessity, so the fact is present/derivable, not withheld. This abstention is itself unverifiable against the texts.
